title: Design Systems That Last
intro: A system is patterns, names and an owner. Without the owner it decays.

learn.title: Two kinds of pattern
learn.text:
**Functional:** the parts people use: buttons, fields, tables.
**Perceptual:** how it feels: type, colour, spacing, motion, voice.

A **shared language** names both, the same in design, code and conversation.

options: A date picker with a calendar grid

learn.title: From parts to pages
learn.text:
**Atoms** (inputs, buttons) → **molecules** (a search form) → **organisms** (a header) → **templates** (layouts) → **pages** (real content).

Real content finds weak spots.

try.q: A label, input and button working as a search form is a:
try.explain: A small group of atoms acting as one unit.

learn.title: Keep it alive
learn.text:
Run it as a **funded product**.
Write a **governance process**: request, change, approve, retire.
Retire patterns with notice and a replacement.
Keep design and code **in sync**.

try.q: What is the biggest threat to a design system?
try.explain: Systems decay when nobody owns them.

learn.title: Team models
learn.text:
**Solitary:** one team’s library, offered to others.
**Centralised:** a dedicated system team.
**Federated:** designers from several teams decide together.

Whatever the model, someone writes decisions down.

options: It can’t be documented by any single team

test.q: What makes a component library a design system?
options: Principles, names and rules for change
More components and variants for every case
test.explain: The library is only one part.

test.q: A homepage layout with no real content yet is a:
test.explain: Pages are templates with real content.

test.q: How should a pattern be retired?
options: With notice and a recommended replacement
Left in place, unsupported and undocumented
Its own team’s needs come first
test.explain: Others fork it when it doesn’t fit.

test.q: Who should a design system serve?
options: Front-end engineers who build the components only
test.explain: Voice, principles and usage matter too.

test.q: How do you start a design system?
options: A small pilot that shows value
test.explain: Prove it, then ask for support.
